prompt: The graph and table below give information about water use worldwide and water consumption in two different countries.
guideHtml:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT IELTS TASK 1

1. Dạng bài

  • Mixed charts: Line graph + Table
  • Nội dung: global water use + country comparison

2. Introduction (công thức)

  • line graph + table + water use + sectors + countries + time

→ dùng: illustrate / compare / show

3. Overview (ý chính, không số)

  • Water use: tăng liên tục ở cả 3 lĩnh vực
  • Agriculture: cao nhất toàn bộ
  • Domestic: thấp nhất
  • Brazil: cao hơn Congo ở tất cả chỉ số

4. Body 1 – Line graph

Agriculture

  • luôn cao nhất
  • tăng mạnh, đặc biệt sau 1950

Industrial

  • tăng đều
  • đứng thứ 2

Domestic

  • thấp nhất
  • tăng chậm

→ Key idea:

  • tất cả đều tăng
  • agriculture chiếm ưu thế

5. Body 2 – Table

So sánh Brazil vs Congo:

Population

  • Brazil lớn hơn nhiều

Irrigated land

  • Brazil vượt trội

Water per person

  • Brazil cao hơn đáng kể

→ Key idea:

  • Brazil cao hơn ở mọi khía cạnh

6. Từ vựng cần dùng

  • dominate
  • increase dramatically
  • rise steadily
  • remain the lowest
  • significantly higher than
  • in all categories
sampleHtml:
The line graph shows global water use in agriculture, industry and domestic sectors between 1900 and 2000, while the table compares water consumption in Brazil and the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2000.

Overall, water use increased significantly in all sectors over the century, with agriculture consistently accounting for the largest share. Additionally, Brazil recorded far higher water consumption and agricultural capacity than Congo.

Agricultural water use rose dramatically from about 500 km³ in 1900 to approximately 3,000 km³ in 2000. Industrial use also increased steadily, from around 100 km³ to about 1,200 km³ by the end of the period. Domestic consumption showed the smallest growth, rising gradually from roughly 50 km³ to just over 300 km³.

In 2000, Brazil had a population of 176 million, compared to only 5.2 million in Congo. The area of irrigated land in Brazil was vastly larger, at 26,500 km², whereas Congo had just 100 km². Consequently, water consumption per person in Brazil was significantly higher, at 359 m³, compared to only 8 m³ in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
chartDescription:
TYPE: mixed
TITLE: Global water use by sector; Water consumption in Brazil and Congo in 2000
UNITS/AXES: Line graph: Y-axis: km³, 0 to 3,000 in increments of 1,000; X-axis: Year, 1900 to 2000 in increments of 10. Table: Population, Irrigated land, Water consumption per person.
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Line graph: Agriculture, Industrial use, Domestic use. Table: Country, Population, Irrigated land, Water consumption per person; Brazil, Democratic Republic of Congo.
DATA:
Agriculture: 1900: 500 km³; 1910: 600 km³; 1920: 700 km³; 1930: 800 km³; 1940: 900 km³; 1950: 1,100 km³; 1960: 1,400 km³; 1970: 1,700 km³; 1980: 2,200 km³; 1990: 2,600 km³; 2000: 2,900 km³.
Industrial use: 1900: 100 km³; 1910: 150 km³; 1920: 200 km³; 1930: 250 km³; 1940: 300 km³; 1950: 400 km³; 1960: 500 km³; 1970: 700 km³; 1980: 900 km³; 1990: 1,200 km³; 2000: 1,500 km³.
Domestic use: 1900: 50 km³; 1910: 70 km³; 1920: 100 km³; 1930: 120 km³; 1940: 150 km³; 1950: 200 km³; 1960: 250 km³; 1970: 300 km³; 1980: 400 km³; 1990: 500 km³; 2000: 600 km³.
Brazil: Population: 176 million; Irrigated land: 26,500 km²; Water consumption per person: 359 m³.
Democratic Republic of Congo: Population: 5.2 million; Irrigated land: 100 km²; Water consumption per person: 8 m³.

KEY FEATURES:
*   Global water use increased significantly across all sectors from 1900 to 2000.
*   Agriculture consistently accounted for the largest share of water use throughout the period.
*   Industrial use showed the second highest increase, while domestic use remained the lowest.
*   In 2000, Brazil had a much larger population, significantly more irrigated land, and substantially higher water consumption per person compared to the Democratic Republic of Congo.
*   The water consumption per person in Brazil was over 40 times higher than in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2000.
